incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated tail latency observed on dedicated-pool-2 (streaming endpoints). p95 ~ 720ms, p99 ~ 3.2s, error rate ~0.6%. Queue depth jumped from 40 -> 600 in ~2m. Paging eric (oncall). Severity: Sev2.

eric (oncall): ack. I'm on it. Can someone post autoscaler + node registration logs and any recent deploys?

maria (sre): i'm pulling the autoscaler timeline. No deploys in the last 30m. Autoscaler shows scale-up triggered at 1918765480 but new nodes didn't become Ready until ~1918765570. that's ~90s registration lag.

jin (runtime): also seeing increased KV cache miss rate and streaming stalls matching the same window. many streaming sessions hit a stall waiting on warm-up / kv fetch.

samir (infra): grabbing logs now. paste of relevant bits:
```
[1918765479] autoscaler: desired=8 current=6 triggered_by=queue_depth
[1918765481] provisioner: starting instance i-0a3... (type=gpu-rtx6000)
[1918765510] bootstrap: running warmup script /opt/warmup/init.sh
[1918765555] node-registration: failed healthcheck: /healthz timed out
[1918765570] node-registration: node i-0a3... registered, joined pool
```

eric (oncall): looks like warmup healthcheck transiently failing. any error lines from warmup script? could be oss-agent timing out on containerd image pull.

samir (infra): found this in bootstrap logs: `curl http://local-metadata/ready` timed out repeatedly while image was being pulled. network IO for image layers spiked, causing health probe timeouts.

jin (runtime): that aligns with streaming stalls. When new nodes are in the process of joining, requests are queued on dedicated-pool-2. Because prefix/KV cache is cold on new nodes, we saw a lot of backend rehydration which lengthened token latencies and caused p99 spikes.

eric (oncall): mitigation plan (short-term): 1) force-add warm instances already with cache prewarmed (if available) 2) temporarily divert non-critical streaming traffic to best-effort-hosting 3) reduce concurrency per connection for streaming to avoid head-of-line stalls 4) apply a conservative internal rate-limit for small-tenant traffic. Who can run these?

maria (sre): i can flip routing for non-critical streaming -> best-effort. doing traffic split 80/20 now.

lina (cs): notifying impacted customers: two enterprise tenants reported slow interactive replies; i've messaged both and offered status update. one asked for ETA.

jin (runtime): quick config we can apply: set `streaming.max_concurrency=4` for dedicated-pool-2 and enable `fallback_model=redwood-alpha-quant` for sessions with latency > 1s. Patch to runtime config applied (rolling):
```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/dedicated-pool-2/config
{ "streaming": { "max_concurrency": 4, "fallback_model": "redwood-alpha-quant" } }
```

samir (infra): manually provisioned 2 warmed nodes from warm-pool and attached to dedicated-pool-2. nodes registered at ~1918765610. routing now includes those nodes.

eric (oncall): thanks. ops-bot, can you throttle onboarding of new sessions to the pool until we confirm warm cache hit rates?

ops-bot: Executing: `redwoodctl pool throttle --pool dedicated-pool-2 --new-sessions 0.5` -> OK

maria (sre): rolling p95/p99 numbers: before mitigation p95=720ms p99=3.2s; after routing + prewarmed nodes p95=260ms p99=710ms. error rate down to 0.12%. still watching.

eric (oncall): good improvement. root cause hypothesis summary: provisioning + image pull / warmup healthcheck delays caused a gap where provisioned capacity wasn't available to absorb burst. cold KV cache on newly registered nodes amplified token latency for streaming workloads (head-of-line stalls). autoscaler triggered correctly but registration latency caused SLO breach.

jin (runtime): follow-ups: - add prewarm-on-provision to ensure KV worker warms within Xs - add canary checkpoint to fail-fast on unhealthy warmup to avoid partial registration - metric to alert on node-registration-lag > 30s (now at 90s) - consider using cached image layers / local registry to reduce image-pull time.

samir (infra): infra action items: - move warm pool closer to provisioner regionally - increase image pull concurrency on bootstrap - change healthcheck grace period to allow image pulls but gate registration until internal services responsive.

maria (sre): ops action items (short-term): - keep routing split until next oncall confirms stable - add temporary synthetic load to verify tail latency under similar queue depths - create a runbook entry for "scale-up registration lag" and attach mitigation commands.

lina (cs): i've opened a customer status note with the two affected tenants and shared ETA ~20-30m for full recovery. they accepted the mitigation update.

eric (oncall): i'm going to mark this as "mitigated" while we watch for 30m. leaving handoff notes for next oncall (maria) at 06:00 PT. If p99 rises above 1.2s or queue depth > 200 please re-pager. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: state=mitigated, p95=250ms p99=680ms queue_depth=45. Incident will be monitored.

eric (oncall): handoff -> maria (sre). Full notes: cause hypothesis, actions taken (force-attached warm nodes, routing split, runtime fallback), follow-ups assigned to infra/jin.

maria (sre): acked. i'll own the follow-ups and confirm infra changes tomorrow. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Closing temporary throttles and reverting traffic-split when stable.
